a wire missing C by 1 mm      : max reciprocal product with the three rotations 0.0010 -> NOT in it (it would resist a rotation)

Outside FACT (the chapter keeps to kinematics, p. 82): sizing for the flower's struts.

motion at each ball: the six leg lengths are constant over the day (both rings are defined from the head pose), so the balls turn only with the loop's corrections: the production runs used 7 mm at most (0.40 deg at the calyx end); the loop's clip is +-40 mm (2.28 deg for one leg at full stroke) and is a design variable of the joint
load per leg: 2031 N at the runs' logged maximum strut force (5.0 kN), 5697 N at the 40 m/s survival gust (14 kN per strut).

a flexure element on the leg does not bend in pure bending: the body's rotation theta about C also moves the element's end by theta x s, and the curvature at the worst end is (1 + 6 s_mid/L) theta/L, s_mid the element's mid-length from C (a leg element that starts at C has s_mid = L/2 and the factor 4).
a Ti wire leg d 6 mm, 60 mm long from C, at the clip's 2.3 deg: bending 876 MPa, Euler 19.19 kN (SF 3.37 at survival), axial 52 MN/m: fails
a Ti wire leg d 6 mm, 300 mm long from C, at the clip's 2.3 deg: bending 175 MPa, Euler 0.77 kN (SF 0.13 at survival), axial 10 MN/m: fails
a Ti wire leg d 4 mm, 300 mm long from C, at the clip's 2.3 deg: bending 117 MPa, Euler 0.15 kN (SF 0.03 at survival), axial 5 MN/m: fails

so a wire tripod cannot carry the survival compression at any length that bends; step 4's equivalence puts two stacked blades per leg. Sizing them: bending under 0.5 sigma_y at the loop's clip, SF 3 on Euler at survival, the joint's axial stiffness as high as the geometry allows (two joints in series with the strut), and the clip reduced until a blade exists:
clip +-40 mm (2.28 deg): no blade meets bending and buckling at once
clip +-30 mm (1.71 deg): stiffest feasible blade t 1.0 x w 120 x L 50 mm, joint 266 MN/m = 1.44 x the strut's EA/L
clip +-20 mm (1.14 deg): stiffest feasible blade t 1.0 x w 120 x L 30 mm, joint 443 MN/m = 2.41 x the strut's EA/L
clip +-15 mm (0.86 deg): stiffest feasible blade t 0.8 x w 120 x L 20 mm, joint 531 MN/m = 2.89 x the strut's EA/L
clip +-10 mm (0.57 deg): stiffest feasible blade t 2.0 x w 120 x L 30 mm, joint 886 MN/m = 4.81 x the strut's EA/L
clip +-5 mm (0.29 deg): stiffest feasible blade t 0.8 x w 120 x L 8 mm, joint 1329 MN/m = 7.22 x the strut's EA/L

chosen: the smallest feasible clip at least twice the runs' usage, +-15 mm (0.86 deg, 2.1 x what the runs used); blade Ti 6Al-4V t 0.8 mm, w 120 mm, free length 20 mm, the pair at 13 and 36 mm from C (factors 5 and 12): outer blade 388 MPa, Euler 55.6 kN (SF 9.8 at survival), axial stiffness per blade 528 MN/m

the joint: 531 MN/m axially = 2.89 x the strut's EA/L 184 MN/m; two joints leave the leg at 59 % of its stiffness and the crown's 16 Hz at 12.3 Hz; at the runs' actual rotation the same blades see 181 MPa

image walk from the joints' compliance at the runs' maximum strut force: 0.10 mm at F per leg; twelve joints, 72 blades, no bearings, no backlash, no lubrication; the loop's clip becomes +-15 mm in both simulations.
